```sql
-- Migration: Split full_name → first_name/last_name (idempotent)
BEGIN;

-- Add new columns
ALTER TABLE users 
ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name VARCHAR(255),
ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name VARCHAR(255);

-- Backfill: split on first space. No space → all to first_name, empty last_name
UPDATE users
SET 
  first_name = COALESCE(first_name,
    CASE 
      WHEN full_name IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN position(' ' IN full_name) = 0 THEN full_name
      ELSE substring(full_name, 1, position(' ' IN full_name) - 1)
    END),
  last_name = COALESCE(last_name,
    CASE 
      WHEN full_name IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN position(' ' IN full_name) = 0 THEN ''
      ELSE substring(full_name, position(' ' IN full_name) + 1)
    END)
WHERE first_name IS NULL;

-- Drop old column
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS full_name;

COMMIT;
```

Idempotent via: `IF NOT EXISTS`/`IF EXISTS` (re-run skips existing columns/drops), `COALESCE` (re-run skips already-filled rows via `WHERE first_name IS NULL`). PostgreSQL; switch `position()` / `substring()` to your DB (SQL Server: `CHARINDEX()`, `SUBSTRING()`; MySQL: `LOCATE()`, `SUBSTRING()`). To enforce NOT NULL after backfill completes, add `ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN first_name SET NOT NULL;` after the update if your migration framework runs idempotently per env (not per deploy).
